text:
A farmer’s old donkey fell into a deep, dry well. The animal cried out in distress for hours while the farmer paced around the edge, wondering what to do.

He eventually concluded that the donkey was too old to be worth saving, and the well was already useless and overdue for filling in. He called his neighbours, and together they began shovelling earth into the well to bury both problems at once.

At first, the donkey panicked. But gradually, as the dirt landed on its back, it noticed something. Each time a load of earth fell on it, it shook the dirt off and stepped up onto the new layer.

“Shake it off and step up,” it repeated to itself. “Shake it off and step up.”

The neighbours kept shovelling, and the donkey kept climbing. The pile beneath its feet grew higher and higher, until finally, exhausted but unharmed, the donkey stepped over the edge of the well and trotted away.

The farmer and his neighbours stared in astonishment.

What had been intended to bury the donkey had become the very thing that saved it.

When the farmer later told the story in the village, an old woman nodded. “Life will often throw dirt at you,” she said. “If you let it pile up on your back, you’ll be buried. But if you shake it off and use it as a step, even your troubles can lift you higher.”

Moral: Every problem can become a stepping stone if we refuse to be buried by it.

The farmer wanted to save the donkey.
What did the donkey do each time earth fell on it?
o: Shook it off and stepped up
